about: I Think I Might Miss My Wife is a moody comic panel of a hard-faced, grey-haired man drawn in heavy black ink against a starry night, with a faint, almost wistful grin creasing his face. A small white speech bubble floats in the dark beside him. In the original the bubble reads "I think I might miss my wife", a sudden flash of soft feeling from a man who looks like he has never felt anything. The template keeps the bubble empty so you can write any late, surprising realization.
usage:
There is one text box, inside the speech bubble on the left. Write a short line that sounds like a quiet confession, ideally something sentimental about something nobody should miss.

It lands with fake nostalgia and late realizations: missing a bad old phone, an annoying coworker, a cancelled show, school lunches or the old version of an app. Keep it to one short sentence; the bubble is small and the contrast with his stone face is the punchline.
ideas: I think I might miss my old phone
I think I might miss the old app layout
I think I might miss school lunches
I think I might miss dial-up
I think I might miss my ex's dog
I think I might miss the old forum
I think I might miss Mondays (no)
